draft.title: What the Renaissance was
card: The Renaissance was a time of new interest in the learning of ancient Greece and Rome. The word means rebirth.
It began in Italy in the 1300s. Many Italian towns had wealthy people who could pay for art and study, and Roman ruins stood all around them.
Thinkers and artists put human abilities at the centre of their work. They studied people, nature and the world, and they valued what humans could learn and make.
Artists copied ideas from Greek and Roman art, such as lifelike bodies. They also tried new methods to show people and places as they really look.
draft.remember: The Renaissance was a rebirth of Greek and Roman learning that began in Italy and focused on human abilities.

a.q: Which statement best describes the Renaissance?
opts: A rebirth of interest in Greek and Roman learning
A war between the towns of Italy and Rome
A new religion that began in Italy in the 1300s
A time when people stopped making art and study
a.why: The Renaissance meant rebirth, and it was a renewed interest in Greek and Roman learning. It was not a new religion: it changed art and study, and it did not replace the faith people already had.
a.clue: Think about what the word rebirth means here.

b.q: Sofia is a painter in Italy in the 1400s. She studies Roman statues and paints people with lifelike bodies. Which idea of the Renaissance does her work show?
opts: Interest in Greek and Roman art and in human abilities
A wish to copy only the art made in her own town
A belief that art should show no real people at all
A plan to end the study of the ancient world
b.why: Sofia studies Roman art and shows human bodies as they look, which reflects the Renaissance interest in Greek and Roman learning and in human abilities. Copying only local art is wrong because Renaissance artists looked back to the ancient world.
b.clue: Look at what Sofia studies and what she paints.

a.best: A rebirth of interest in Greek and Roman learning

b.best: Interest in Greek and Roman art and in human abilities

proposal.title: What the Renaissance was

a.q: Historians call the Renaissance a rebirth. What was reborn?
opts: Interest in the learning of ancient Greece and Rome
The rule of the Roman Empire over all of Italy
The Christian faith, which had nearly died out
Interest in the castles and knights of the past
a.why: Renaissance thinkers and artists turned back to the learning of ancient Greece and Rome. It was not the return of Roman rule: the change came in art and study, not in who governed Italy.
a.clue: Was the change in ideas and learning, or in who ruled?

b.q: Sofia is a painter in Italy in the 1400s. She studies Roman statues and paints people with lifelike bodies. Which idea of the Renaissance does her work show?
opts: Interest in ancient art and in showing people as they look
A turn away from the ancient world toward new subjects
A belief that art should show heaven, not the real world
A wish to follow only the art traditions of her own town
b.why: Sofia looks back to Roman art and shows human bodies as they really look, which reflects the Renaissance interest in Greek and Roman learning and in people. A turn away from the ancient world is wrong, because she is studying Roman statues.
b.clue: Look at what Sofia studies and what she paints.

a.best: Interest in the learning of ancient Greece and Rome

b.best: Interest in ancient art and in showing people as they look
